refactor(notifications): classify NotificationFeedBloc invariants as Reportable (#4616)

Per .claude/rules/error_handling.md decision matrix, narrow the broad
`catch (e, s)` arm at six addError sites in NotificationFeedBloc into:

  - `on Exception catch (e, s)` — matrix-NO domain failures
    (FunnelcakeException, Drift IO, follow-repo auth/relay-IO),
    behavior unchanged.
  - `catch (e, s)` — matrix-YES invariant violations
    (StateError, TypeError, RangeError), wrapped with
    Reportable(e, context: NotificationFeedBlocReportableSites.xxx)
    so DivineBlocObserver forwards them to Crashlytics.

All recovery emits, optimistic-rollback semantics, and existing test
expectations are preserved. 6 new blocTests verify the Reportable arm
fires on Error throws (24 tests total, was 18).

Follow-up to PR #4599 (comment-only matrix classification).
Closes #4603. Part of epic #4336.

feat(c2pa): make CAWG "do not train" assertion unconditional (#4613)

* feat(c2pa): make CAWG training-mining opt-out unconditional (#4611)

Every published video now unconditionally carries the
`cawg.training-mining` assertion marking AI training, inference,
generative training, and data mining as `notAllowed`. The opt-in
code path is removed so this becomes platform policy rather than a
toggleable default — there is no UI to flip it off and no Riverpod
provider to read.

Why: a per-user toggle weakens the signal for every other creator
on Divine. Keeping the assertion unconditional makes the
declaration unambiguous and verifiable across all content, which
is the value of a cryptographically signed line in the sand even
when scrapers ignore it (like robots.txt).

Adds `mobile/docs/AI_TRAINING_POLICY.md` explaining the policy and
its scope.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(c2pa): align AI training policy docs with runtime behavior

feat(recorder/library): clip trash bin with 30-day retention (#4546)

* feat(db): add soft-delete column to clips table for trash bin

Adds `deleted_at` nullable timestamp column on `clips` plus an index,
runtime ADD COLUMN IF MISSING for existing databases, and DAO methods
(softDeleteClip, restoreClip, getTrashedLibraryClips,
watchTrashedLibraryClips, getTrashedClipsOlderThan). Existing read paths
(getAllClips, getLibraryClips, getClipsByDraftId, watchLibraryClips,
watchClipsByDraftId, getCountByDraftId) now exclude trashed rows.

Foundation for clip trash bin: recorder/library deletes will move
clips to trash instead of hard-deleting, with 30-day retention.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(clip-library): soft-delete via ClipLibraryService trash methods

Splits ClipLibraryService.deleteClip into softDelete, restore, and
hardDelete + purgeExpiredTrash + getTrashedClips. softDelete optionally
clears draftId so a recorder-trashed clip lands in the library on
restore rather than a stale session.

ClipsLibraryBloc now routes both single and batch delete events through
softDelete, captures the deleted IDs in lastDeletedClipIds for snackbar
Undo, and gains four new events: TrashLoadRequested, RestoreClips,
HardDeleteClip, EmptyTrash, plus trashedClips on state.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(recorder): replace destructive undo with soft-delete + snackbar Undo

Recorder's bottom-left button now schedules a soft-delete of the last
clip (with draftId cleared) and shows a "Clip moved to trash • Undo"
snackbar for 5 seconds. Tapping Undo restores the clip to its original
position; ignoring the snackbar lets the clip sit in trash where
30-day retention takes over.

ClipManagerNotifier tracks the pending deletion in state so the UI
reflects it immediately, and commits-on-addClip / commits-on-reorder
/ commits-on-clear so a fresh recording never leaks a half-undone
state. Icon swapped from arrowCounterClockwise to trash to match the
actual destructive semantics.

New shared helper clip_delete_snackbar.dart wires both capture and
classic recording modes to the same UX. Existing tests updated to
use the new schedule/restore API surface.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(library): trash bin screen + 30-day auto-purge

Adds a Recently Deleted screen (LibraryTrashScreen) accessed from a
new trash icon on the clips library toolbar. Lists soft-deleted clips
with per-item Restore and Delete-now actions plus a single "Empty
trash" action when non-empty. Closing the screen reloads the library
so restores show up immediately.

Wires purgeExpiredTrash() into the app-startup lifecycle handler so
clips past the 30-day retention window are hard-deleted on next
launch. Best-effort, idempotent, never blocks startup.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* i18n(clip-trash): translate trash bin keys into all 17 locales

Adds full translations for videoRecorderClipUndoLabel, libraryTrashTitle,
libraryTrashEmptyTitle, libraryTrashEmptySubtitle, libraryTrashRestoreLabel,
libraryTrashDeleteNowLabel, libraryTrashEmptyAllLabel, and
libraryTrashEntryLabel across am, ar, bg, de, es, fil, fr, id, it, ja,
ko, nl, pl, pt, ro, sv, tr. Updates videoRecorderClipDeletedMessage in
each locale to match the new "Clip moved to trash" English copy.

Drops the corresponding allowlist entries from arb_consistency_test —
the gate now enforces full coverage on these keys instead of accepting
English fallback.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(db): drop dartdoc cross-refs that fail strict comment_references

DB Client CI runs flutter analyze with infos-as-fatal, and [name]
bracket references to column getters or other-method parameters fail
the comment_references lint when the name isn't visible at the doc-
comment scope. Switched those references to backticked code spans so
the doc reads the same but the lint no longer flags them.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(library): drop confirm dialog, wire undo snackbar, show purge countdown

Self-review pass on the clip-trash-bin PR:

1. Drop the library delete confirm dialog. With a 30-day trash bin in
   place, the dialog was both lying ("permanently removed from your
   device") and double-paying for safety on top of the trash. The
   recorder path already skips confirm; library now matches. Removed
   the orphaned `libraryDelete*` ARB keys from every locale.

2. Wire the dead `lastDeletedClipIds` field into the library snackbar.
   "N clips deleted" now shows an Undo action that dispatches
   `ClipsLibraryRestoreClips` on the bloc, surfacing the soft-delete /
   restore round-trip the field was already populating.

3. Plumb `clips.deleted_at` from the Drift row through the service

   "Auto-deletes in N days" (ICU plural, locales today/tomorrow/in N)

   constant lives on `ClipLibraryService.trashRetention` so the
   countdown and the purge sweep can't drift apart.

Nits: wrap the startup `purgeExpiredTrash` await in try/catch to honor
the "best-effort" comment; drop the no-op `onTap`/`onLongPress` on the
trash thumbnail (made the callbacks nullable on `VideoClipThumbnailCard`).

commit.message:
feat(notifications): mark all read on leave and fix mark-read sync (#4573)

* feat(notifications): mark all as read when the user leaves the screen

When a user opens the notifications surface (either the standalone
/notifications route or the Notifications segment inside the inbox)
and then leaves it — bottom-nav tab switch, segment toggle to
Messages, or auth flip — every visible notification is now flipped
to read and the badge collapses to zero. New unread arrivals after
that point bump the badge normally via the existing realtime /
refresh paths.

Implementation: a small MarkAllReadOnDispose stateful wrapper fires
`NotificationRepository.markAllAsRead()` once in dispose(). The
repository already does the optimistic snapshot flip + server write
+ rollback on failure (PR #4034 semantics), so the badge cubit and
feed bloc recover consistently if the API call fails.

Why dispose and not on open: mark-on-open would hide brand-new
notifications the user hadn't actually seen yet — the existing
"does not mark on open" test still pins that contract.

Why a wrapper instead of a bloc event: the repository call must
survive the BlocProvider being torn down with the route, and the
repository instance outlives the bloc.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(notifications): make mark-read actually persist server-side

The notifications badge has been bouncing back up after every
mark-as-read since #4271 — the optimistic snapshot flip works,
the API call goes out, the server processes it, the client throws
on the response, and the repository's catch-block rolls back the
snapshot. Three independent bugs combined to make this happen, all
on the same POST /api/users/{pubkey}/notifications/read endpoint:

1. **Response shape mismatch.** Per the funnelcake LLM-guide the
   real server response is `{"marked_count": N, "marked_all": bool}`
   — there is no `success` field. PR #4271's
   `MarkReadResponse.fromJson` defaulted `success` to `false`
   when absent, so the client misread every successful 200 as a
   `success: false` soft-failure and threw
   `FunnelcakeApiException("rejected by server")`. Existing tests
   passed because their fixtures synthetically sent `success: true`.
   Now: honor an explicit `success` value if the server ever adopts
   the field, otherwise derive it from the absence of `error`.

2. **NIP-98 URL mismatch.** The repository signed the *path*
   (`/api/users/.../notifications/read`) while the request went to
   the *full URL* (`https://api.divine.video/api/users/.../...`).
   NIP-98 requires the auth event's `u` tag to match the
   server-visible URL exactly. The new `notificationsReadUri()`
   helper exposes the same URL the client posts to so the repo
   signs it consistently.

3. **NIP-98 payload hash mismatch.** The auth callback was called
   with `(url, method)` — no body. `nip98_auth_service.dart` then
   hashed the empty string while the request body was `{}` or
   `{"notification_ids": [...]}`. Threaded a `body` parameter
   through the `AuthHeadersProvider` typedef and the
   `notification_repository_provider` wiring so
   `createAuthToken(payload: body)` receives the exact bytes the
   request will send. The new
   `FunnelcakeApiClient.buildMarkNotificationsReadBody()` helper
   produces the body in one place so the repository and the client
   can't drift.

Each bug independently caused the symptom — the badge could only
"stay at 0" if all three lined up. With the on-leave dispose hook
from the first commit, the failure was hit every time the user
navigated away from notifications, making it impossible to miss.

Tests:
- `funnelcake_api_client_notification_test`: fixtures rewritten
  to match the documented server shape; new test pins the
  no-`success`-field success path.
- `notification_response_test`: new tests for the no-`success`,
  explicit-`success`, and `error`-present paths.
- `notification_repository_test`: existing 9 `authHeadersProvider`
  call sites updated to the `({body})` signature; two new tests
  verify the full URL + JSON body get signed.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(notifications): key BlocProvider on repository identity

Per `.claude/rules/state_management.md`, a `BlocProvider.create:` that
consumes an identity-flippable Riverpod dependency must carry a
`ValueKey` over that dependency so the bloc rebuilds when the captured
value swaps. Both notifications pages were missing this contract.

`InboxNotificationsPage` worked in practice because the upstream
`KeyedSubtree(key: ValueKey('notifications-$currentPubkey'))` in
`inbox_view.dart:97-100` forces the whole subtree to remount on
pubkey change. The standalone `NotificationsPage` under
`/notifications/:index` has no such wrapper — and once PR #4573's
`MarkAllReadOnDispose` lands, the missing key opens a silent
mark-all-read-on-wrong-user path on account switch: the persisted
`State<MarkAllReadOnDispose>` updates its `widget.repository` to the
new user's repo via Flutter's normal widget update, then `dispose()`
later fires `markAllAsRead()` against the new user's account, even
though the previous user was the one actually viewing.

Adds `key: ValueKey(notificationRepository)` to the BlocProvider in
both pages and pins the contract with a repo-swap test that mirrors
`conversation_page_repo_swap_test.dart` (DM analogue, #3503).
Relates to epic #4200.

mark-as-read since #4271 — the optimistic snapshot flip works,
the API call goes out, the server processes it, the client throws
on the response, and the repository's catch-block rolls back the
snapshot. Three independent bugs combined to make this happen, all
on the same POST /api/users/{pubkey}/notifications/read endpoint:

   `MarkReadResponse.fromJson` defaulted `success` to `false`

   `success: false` soft-failure and threw

   passed because their fixtures synthetically sent `success: true`.

   the field, otherwise derive it from the absence of `error`.

   the *full URL* (`https://api.divine.video/api/users/.../...`).

   server-visible URL exactly. The new `notificationsReadUri()`
   helper exposes the same URL the client posts to so the repo
   signs it consistently.

   with `(url, method)` — no body. `nip98_auth_service.dart` then
   hashed the empty string while the request body was `{}` or
   `{"notification_ids": [...]}`. Threaded a `body` parameter
   through the `AuthHeadersProvider` typedef and the

   request will send. The new

   can't drift.

both pages and pins the contract with a repo-swap test that mirrors

fix(crashlytics): guard fire-and-forget Bloc addError calls against post-close races (#4605) (#4608)

* fix(welcome): guard _hydrateAccount addError against post-close race

_hydrateProfiles is dispatched fire-and-forget from _onWelcomeStarted
and iterates Future.wait over _hydrateAccount. If the user navigates
away from the welcome screen before the in-flight Drift getProfile
calls resolve, the bloc closes — and the addError added in #4592
fires on a closed BlocBase, throwing StateError that surfaces as
nonfatal Crashlytics noise.

Wrap the addError call in `if (!isClosed)`. The local Log.warning
above stays unguarded — it remains safe regardless of close state and
preserves triage visibility.

Adds a regression test that holds the in-flight getProfile open via a
Completer, closes the bloc, then completes the future with an error,
asserting that no error reaches the BlocObserver post-close.

Refs #4605.

* fix(clips-library): guard _recoverAndReload addError against post-close race

_recoverAndReload is launched fire-and-forget via unawaited() from
_onLoadRequested. The sibling add(ClipsLibraryLoadRequested) is
already !isClosed-guarded; the asymmetric addError call in the catch
arm could still fire on a closed bloc when recoverMissingAssets
errors after the user navigates away from the clip library.

Wrap the addError call in `if (!isClosed)` for symmetry with the
existing add() guard.

Adds a regression test that holds recoverMissingAssets open via a
Completer, closes the bloc, then completes the future with an error,
asserting that no error reaches the BlocObserver post-close.

Refs #4605.

* fix(video-interactions): guard publish addError against post-close race

Audit-discovered sites under #4605: both _publishLike and
_publishRepost run fire-and-forget via unawaited() and previously
called addError without an isClosed guard. The sibling add() in each
method is already !isClosed-gated (lines 299 and 418), so the
asymmetric addError could fire on a closed bloc when the user
scrolls the feed mid-publish and tears down the per-video bloc.

Wrap both addError calls in `if (!isClosed)` for symmetry with the
existing add() guards.

Adds two regression tests that hold toggleLike / toggleRepost open
via Completers, close the bloc, then complete the futures with an
error, asserting that no error reaches the BlocObserver post-close.

Refs #4605.

* refactor: tighten fire-and-forget guard comments

Self-review: the original 5-9 line comments restated context that is
already in the issue body and commit message. Shorten to 2-3 lines per
code_style.md, keeping the load-bearing WHY (sibling add() symmetry,
post-close StateError) and dropping the issue-number reference (git
log carries it).

No behavior change.

feat(keycast): mid-session token refresh on 401 and app resume (#4589)

* feat(keycast): add mid-session token refresh on 401 and app resume

Keycast OAuth tokens expire after ~3 hours. Users who leave the app
backgrounded (common with iOS background modes for push notifications)
return to a stale token and all RPC-backed operations (reporting, signing,
encryption) fail silently.

Two recovery paths:

A) On app resume, check if the stored OAuth session has expired and
   proactively refresh it before any RPC call is attempted.

B) In KeycastRpc._call(), detect 401 responses and invoke a
   TokenRefreshCallback to obtain a fresh access token, then retry the
   request once. This catches tokens that expire mid-session without
   an intervening app backgrounding.

Both paths share the same refresh mechanism via OAuthClient.refreshSession().

Closes #4588

* fix(keycast): deduplicate token refresh to prevent race conditions

Code review caught that _refreshOAuthTokenOnResume and _refreshAccessToken
both independently call refreshSession(), which can double-consume a
one-time-use refresh token when they race (app resume + concurrent 401).

Fix: introduce _pendingTokenRefresh singleton Future (same pattern as the
existing _pendingRefresh) so concurrent callers share a single in-flight
refresh. Also adds try/catch around the unawaited resume refresh call and
reconstructs _keycastSigner on resume so its internal token is fresh.

* refactor(auth): consolidate OAuth refresh into single-flight helper

All code paths that need a fresh KeycastSession now go through
_refreshOAuthSession() instead of calling _oauthClient.refreshSession()
directly. This prevents double-spending rotating refresh tokens when
401 retry, app resume, init recovery, and background upgrade race, and
ensures userPubkey is bound before the session is persisted.

* fix(auth): bind refreshed OAuth session to expected owner, not active profile

_doRefreshOAuthSession() used _currentProfile?.publicKeyHex to bind
userPubkey on the refreshed session. During account transitions, this
could bind account B's session to account A if A is still the active
profile. Thread expectedOwnerPubkey from callers that hold the stored
session, falling back to _currentProfile for true mid-session refreshes.

* fix(auth): thread expectedOwnerPubkey through signInForAccount paths

signInForAccount has pubkeyHex for the target account — pass it to
_tryRefreshOAuthSession and _upgradeDivineRpcInBackground so the
refreshed session binds to the requested account, not _currentProfile
which may still point to the previous account during a switch.

* style: fix dart format in auth_service.dart

* fix: bind userPubkey in refreshSession before first save

Pass userPubkey into KeycastOAuth.refreshSession() so the session is
owner-bound before _saveSession() persists it. This eliminates the
window where storage held an unbound session between the OAuth
client's save and AuthService's subsequent save.

* fix(test): update mock stubs for refreshSession userPubkey parameter

The production code now passes userPubkey to refreshSession(), but
test mocks only stubbed the no-argument form. In mocktail, an
explicitly passed null named parameter doesn't match a stub without
that parameter. Also fixes the "refresh succeeds" test timeout by
providing a userPubkey on the refreshed session (preventing a real
HTTP call to getPublicKey) and adding a storage side-effect to the
mock (matching what the real refreshSession does internally).
